Existing sessions kept the ends they were created with; the document says so. |

| **7.4.1** Verify that when session termination is triggered (such as logout or expiration), the application disallows any further use of the session. | **7.4.2** Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted (such as an employee leaving the company). | L1 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.4.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/approval.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/user-admin.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/user-admin.ts)<br>doc [docs/security/sessions.md](../../../docs/security/sessions.md) | sessions.resolve refuses a session whose user is not active or is deleted, on every uncached lookup. Rejecting a user revokes all their sessions in the same transaction, and every path that ends sessions (logout, log out everywhere, ending one from the list, the administrators' termination, rejecting an account, deactivating one) empties this process's cache entries at once; the cache is not left to run out. M5 sprint 3 added the account-disable feature this note asked for: POST /users/{id}/deactivate (core.identity.user.deactivate) sets the status deactivated and calls sessions.revokeAll with the transaction of the status change and its event, so a failure of either undoes both (user-admin.test.ts proves the sessions end with the status and, with the outbox broken, that nothing changes; admin-users-routes.test.ts shows through the pipeline that the old cookie and the second browser's cookie answer 401, that a sign-in answers like a wrong password, and that an access token of the account stops working). Across server processes a session may still be accepted for at most the 5 s cache TTL (docs/security/sessions.md, ADR-0007); there is no cross-process invalidation, and a verified access token is trusted for its own short cache TTL. |

The Playwright tests in apps/web/e2e/navigation.spec.ts sign in through the API as a plain User and as an Admin, read GET /ui/navigation, visit every link and every page without a parameter plus an error page, and find the control on each, under BASE_PATH / and /a/b; a second test uses the control and shows that the old cookie is then refused (401 from the API, a page with nobody signed in). Not shown by the test: a page with a :param segment is visited only when a link leads to it; in sprint 1 every page of the navigation is public, so the walk reaches pages that need a sign-in only as later sprints register them (it reads the list from the API and needs no change); and a module that rendered its own chrome outside the layout would not be covered, which the architecture does not allow but no lint rule enforces. M5 sprint 4: the same walk reaches the Logs, System and Notification status pages for an Admin (and, with the inbox, the bell and the inbox page for every signed-in user); the pages of core.audit and core.notifications come from their own `ui.routes`, so the list needs no change. |

| **7.5.1** Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, or other information used in account recovery. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.5.1]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/profile.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/profile.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc-link.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc-link.ts)<br>doc [docs/security/sessions.md](../../../docs/security/sessions.md) | Changing the email address (PATCH /account/profile with a new email), starting to link an OIDC identity and confirming the mailed link that finishes a link (POST /account/oidc-link/confirm) ask for a recent authentication (default 5 minutes) in the service and answer 401 reauthentication-required without one; a password change already asks for the current password. The authentication is the password, or a fresh login at the provider with prompt=login, max_age=0 and a checked auth_time. The setting recentAuthSeconds is the window; a reviewer may judge a 5-minute window weaker than a prompt on every change. In the web app (M5) the profile page runs each of these through a dialog that asks for the password first and, for an account that has none (409), for a sign-in at the provider; the Playwright journey apps/web/e2e/reauth.spec.ts ages the session in the database, changes the email address, is refused for a wrong password, and sees the change made after the right one, and apps/web/e2e/oidc.spec.ts does the same through the provider (prompt=login, max_age=0) and shows that the change is repeated after the return and that what the page kept for the way back (session storage, a path and an intent, no secret, ten minutes at most) is gone. Recovery and MFA configuration do not exist as editable attributes yet; a new one must call requireRecentAuth. |
| **7.5.2** Verify that users are able to view and (having authenticated again with at least one factor) terminate any or all currently active sessions. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.5.2]`<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/accounts.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/accounts.ts)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/sessions.ts) | GET /account/sessions lists the caller's own live sessions (id, created, last seen, current; no secret and no device data, which is not stored); DELETE /account/sessions/{id} ends one after a recent authentication, scoped to the caller in the update itself, so another user's id answers like an unknown one; POST /auth/logout-all ends all of them, also after a recent authentication. | **7.6.1** Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties (RPs) and Identity Providers (IdPs) behave as documented, requiring re-authentication as necessary such as when the maximum time between IdP authentication events is reached. | L2 | pass | test `[ASVS-7.6.1]`<br>doc [docs/security/sessions.md](../../../docs/security/sessions.md)<br>code [modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts](../../../modules/core-identity/service/oidc.ts) | docs/security/sessions.md documents how the lifetime and termination of a Scorpion session relate to the provider's: independent after the login, bounded by the absolute lifetime, re-authentication at the provider on demand (prompt=login, max_age=0, auth_time validated). The test shows the behaviour the document describes: an account without a password signs in at the provider again, with prompt=login and max_age=0, and only then may it change its email address; a stale auth_time is refused (6.8.4). Not met in the stronger sense: there is no maximum time between IdP authentication events for an ordinary session, and no back-channel logout; the document says so. A reviewer may judge that insufficient. |
